Title: Trump's White House media ban faces long odds in court
Article:
US President Donald Trump's move to ban several news outlets from the White House over his dislike of their coverage likely runs afoul of US legal prohibitions against viewpoint discrimination by the government, four legal experts told Reuters.
Trump's announcement on Friday that he would ban CNN, MSNOW and Politico for reporting what he deemed "FAKE NEWS" was the latest move by his administration to curtail press access, part of the Republican president's wider pressure campaign against news coverage he dislikes.
Trump said on Saturday that he might ban other outlets as well.
The president's justification for the ban could be its undoing in a legal challenge because US courts have long held that the government cannot condition press access on favourable coverage once it has opened a space to the media, according to legal experts.
"They don't have to allow anyone in, but once they do, they cannot decide who gets in based on viewpoint or content", said University of Maryland journalism professor Lucy Dalglish.
The White House said in a statement that the news outlets were completely capable of reporting from outside the White House.
"The Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President's Oval Office. The lies they smear are a disservice to the American public and tear at the very fabric of our Democracy," the statement said.
In a lawsuit filed in Washington D.C, federal court on Monday, CNN, MSNOW and Politico said the ban was unlawful retaliation for legally protected speech under the First Amendment and violated their rights to due process.
"This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles," the outlets said.
US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who blocked Trump from banning a CNN reporter during his first presidency, scheduled a Wednesday hearing on the outlets' request for a temporary restraining order blocking the move.
The press does not have unfettered access to the White House, and presidents have more discretion over access to tightly controlled spaces with limited capacity, such as the Oval Office and Air Force One.
It is longstanding practice for the White House to select so-called pool reporters who follow the president while he travels and disseminate coverage to other media.
CNN is a member of the TV pool, which suspended coverage on Monday.
[[nid:1539380]]
A Washington D.C, appeals court held in June 2025 that Trump likely had the right to bar the Associated Press from certain spaces including the Oval Office, but not White House press facilities writ large.
Trump had banned the AP from the pool of reporters that cover his movements because it did not adopt the name Gulf of America, his preferred name for the Gulf of Mexico.
A final ruling is still pending.
CNN, MSNOW and Politico said in their lawsuit that their reporters had been denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday and were told their so-called hard passes, which are given to vetted and credentialed media representatives, had been deactivated.
The outlets said they were given no advance notice of the ban or opportunity to contest Trump's decision, which they said violated their right to due process under the Fifth Amendment's protections against unfair treatment by the government.
The government is permitted to restrict reporters if they are deemed security risks but must have a clear basis for doing so and follow established procedures that give reporters the chance to dispute their designation, according to First Amendment lawyer Douglas Mirell.
"There has to be a non-arbitrary and compelling reason to restrict access, and to say that you disagree with someone's opinion has never been a compelling reason under the First Amendment," Mirell said.
In March, a federal judge blocked the US Defence Department from implementing regulations that would allow officials to revoke reporters' Pentagon press credentials if they sought information that was not authorised for public release.
The department said the new rules were aimed at protecting national security.
But the New York Times said in a lawsuit that the changes would permit the Pentagon to ban news outlets over coverage the department viewed as unfavourable.
US District Judge Paul Friedman granted the Times' request for an initial order blocking the policy, saying it violated the First and Fifth Amendments because it was vague, overly expansive and "makes any newsgathering and reporting not blessed by the Department" a possible basis for revocation of a journalist's ​pass.
The Trump administration is appealing the ruling.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court: Boy's acquittal in Bandar Utama murder must not diminish victim's life, family's grief
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The High Court has stressed that its finding that a 15-year-old boy was not criminally responsible for the death of his 16-year-old schoolmate due to unsoundness of mind must not be interpreted as diminishing her life or the grief of her family.
In concluding the grounds of judgment, judge Adlin Abdul Majid said the court's finding of unsoundness of mind and the boy's acquittal of the murder charge did not mean the fatal attack had not occurred or that no one was responsible.
She said the finding was not intended, and should not be understood, to diminish the victim's life or cause anyone to forget her.
"This is not a finding that the act did not happen, or that no one was responsible for it.
"It is a finding that the person who committed the act was at the time in the grip of a serious psychotic illness that had gone unrecognised and untreated for years, and that the law does not hold such a person criminally responsible for conduct he could not, at that moment, appreciate as wrong," she said.
The boy was
acquitted of murdering
the girl after the court found that he was of unsound mind when the incident occurred at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, on Oct 14 last year.
He was ordered to be detained at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for psychiatric treatment at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.
Adlin described the victim as a young student with close family and friends, and a bright future ahead of her.
"Her untimely and tragic death is an immense and irreversible loss to all who knew her.
"Nothing in these findings should be read as suggesting that her death was any less devastating or any less real, because it was brought about by an illness, rather than by malice," she said.
Adlin said that the victim's family continued to bear profound grief, adding that a diagnosis could not diminish their loss.
"The grief of her family is not diminished by a diagnosis and this judgment does not ask it to be," she said.
Adlin said the case had exposed how serious mental illness could progress in a child while remaining invisible to those around him, and the potentially devastating consequences of failing to recognise it.
She said that in this case, symptoms of a severe, early-onset psychotic illness had been present from the age of nine and were documented over five years through family accounts, school records and teachers' observations.
"Yet, never once recognised as an illness. The signs were there — withdrawal, delusional thinking, a refusal to remove his mask, chronic lateness born of fear, and hallucinated voices.
"They were read, understandably, as behavioural or disciplinary problems rather than as a medical emergency.
"The cost of that misreading has now been borne by two families," she said.
Adlin said that if any measure of good could emerge from the tragedy, it should be a greater understanding among parents, schools, the courts and the public of the warning signs and consequences of untreated mental illness in children.
"This is so that symptoms are recognised and treated earlier, and never again permitted to progress unaddressed, to a point of such devastating consequence so that other families may be spared what both these families have suffered.
"It is in this spirit that this decision was made," she said.
The boy was represented by lawyers Kitson Foong and Chew Jee San.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Diving industry backs tighter rules, protection for Sabah guides
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah diving industry players have welcomed the new Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (MOTAC) licensing requirements for dive guides.
Sabah Dive Squad Club president Sim Fui said regulation was important to raise accountability and safety standards.
However, he said it should also protect the livelihoods of Sabah's local dive guides and instructors.
"Registration should therefore create a fair and properly regulated industry where qualified local dive professionals are given priority and are not displaced by unregulated or unauthorised foreign freelance operators.
"Ultimately, we support regulation that achieves three objectives: protecting divers' safety, raising professional standards, and protecting employment opportunities for Sabah's local dive community," he said.
Under Motac's guidelines, new applicants for a scuba diving tourist guide licence must be Malaysian citizens aged at least 18, hold a valid minimum Dive Master or Dive Instructor certification, complete a recognised tourism course and be appointed or employed by a dive centre holding a valid Tourism Operation and Travel Agency Business (TOBTAB) licence.
Applicants must also join a tourist guide association and submit supporting documents, including medical reports, diving certification and proof of appointment by a licensed dive centre.
[[nid:1539366]]
The guideline took effect on April 15, but its requirements only came to the attention of many divers after the Malaysia Scuba Diving Association announced on its Facebook page that it would conduct a one-day course nationwide to help dive professionals prepare for the registration process.
Semporna Diving Professionals Association president Suzimin Edris said the registration system could improve oversight by enabling authorities and dive operators to establish who was properly qualified to work in the industry.
He said the requirement could also ensure dive companies hired registered professionals and met their obligations to contribute to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and Social Security Organisation (Socso), rather than freely engaging freelance workers.
Suzimin said registration could benefit dive professionals by giving them clearer employment opportunities, but called for the application process to be simplified as applicants currently had to prepare numerous documents.
Freelance diving instructor Aquila Chu, 41, who is based in Kota Kinabalu and Semporna, said the growing number of local and foreign instructors made greater structure and supervision necessary.
"At the moment it is really free for all .As the numbers of locals and foreign instructors keep increasing, it's the right direction to move in.
"It's all fun until accidents happen. Some kind of standard and supervision is good for everyone," he said.
However, Aquila remained sceptical about how the new system would be implemented and supervised, stressing that regulation would only be meaningful if it translated into consistent safety standards across the industry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two suffer burns in Bayan Baru restaurant fire
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Two people suffered first-degree burns after a fire broke out in the kitchen of a restaurant in Tingkat Mahsuri, Bayan Baru.
Firefighters received the distress call at 12.19pm.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the fire involved the kitchen area, measuring about 10ft by 15ft (3m by 4.6m), with overall damage estimated at 20 per cent.
"The public had extinguished the fire using a dry powder extinguisher before firefighters arrived.
"The two victims suffered first-degree burns and went to a nearby clinic for treatment," he said.
One victim was a man in his 40s who suffered burns to his legs, while the other was a 47-year-old woman who suffered burns to her hands.
The fire was brought under control at 12.36pm and ended at 1.21pm.
Mopping up operations were conducted to ensure there were no remaining hazards before the case was handed the case over to the Fire Investigation Team.

Title: Rehda seeks stamp duty relief, targted HOC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Enhancing the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) and introducing improved financing structures are among the proposals made by the Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia for the 2027 Budget.
The association is also seeking an extension of existing stamp duty relief and a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) for unsold completed residential units.
Rehda president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the proposals, which have been submitted to the Ministry of Housing and Local Government and the Ministry of Finance, are aimed at addressing constraints faced by homebuyers as well as the rising cost of housing delivery.
He said among the key proposals is an enhancement of the SJKP to widen access to financing, particularly for young Malaysians, the self-employed and those without fixed or conventional incomes.
"Access to housing financing remains a major barrier to house ownership, particularly for young Malaysians, the self-employed and purchasers with low or non-traditional incomes," said Zaini at a media briefing on Rehda's Property Industry Survey for the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) here today.
Rehda also proposed government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms, as well as stepped-up financing structures that would allow lower repayments during the initial years of house ownership.
He said the measures would help prospective buyers who have the capacity to service monthly housing repayments but struggle with the upfront costs of purchasing a home.
Most prospective buyers, especially those in the Bottom 40 (B40) group, have the capacity to service their monthly housing repayments, but they face difficulty accumulating sufficient savings for stamp duty and other initial acquisition costs, said Zaini.
"Normally, coming up with that 10 per cent is difficult for them. So, we are asking the government to help on this," he said.
On stamp duty, Zaini said Rehda proposed extending the existing relief to residential properties priced above RM500,000 and up to RM1 million, with an appropriate tiered relief mechanism for purchases made between January and December 2027.
He said Rehda has also proposed measures to address unsold completed residential units, including a special HOC for such properties that have obtained the Certificate of Completion and Compliance (CCC).
"There are a lot of overhang units, so we want to address these units first," said Zaini.
Rehda's survey indicates that 59 per cent of 181 respondents had unsold completed residential units as of June 30. The reasons cited include rejection of end-financing applications, high property prices, and unreleased Bumiputera units.
He said a targeted HOC could improve market liquidity and allow capital tied up in unsold properties to be recycled into new developments.
Rehda is advocating for data-driven housing planning to better align future housing supply with actual demand, preventing supply-demand mismatches.
Zaini emphasised that reducing the cost of housing delivery is another priority, given rising infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory and compliance costs borne by developers.
"Housing affordability is influenced not only by purchasers' access to financing but also by the cost of developing and delivering homes.
"We are asking the government to look at these costs again. Once these are reduced, developers can also reduce prices significantly," he said.
Rehda is also seeking fiscal incentives to accelerate construction productivity, technology adoption and digitalisation, including incentives for investments in Building Information Modelling, Industrialised Building System, artificial intelligence, automation, software and equipment.
Proposals include accelerated capital allowances and investment tax allowances for qualifying expenditures in these areas.
The association also called for measures to accelerate green and sustainable housing development as part of its 2027 Budget proposals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuala Nerang bomb discovery: Unexploded 60mm mortar round found near Sungai Padang Terap
Article:
KUALA NERANG: A landscaping worker and two colleagues found a mortar round while carrying out maintenance work near Sungai Padang Terap here at 10.30am today.
Padang Terap district police chief Superintendent Mohd Anuar Junoh said police were alerted to the discovery and dispatched a team to the location near Kuala Nerang town for further investigation.
He said the worker and his colleagues were clearing vegetation and removing weeds from a planter box when they found the object.
"Members of the Kedah Contingent Police Headquarters Bomb Disposal Unit (UPB) who inspected the object found it to be a 60mm 'UXO Mortar' round," he said when contacted.
Anuar said the mortar round was subsequently taken by the UPB to a quarry for destruction.

Title: Gunmen kill 11 in South African township
Article:
DURBAN: Gunmen stormed a homestead in a township in South Africa's eastern port city of Durban, killing 11 people, the head of the provincial government and police said on Wednesday.
South Africa is awash with legal and illegal firearms, and shootings are common, often fuelled by gang rivalry and competition between informal businesses.
"The victims, including a pregnant woman, were gathered at a house shortly before 11pm (2100 GMT Tuesday) when armed assailants reportedly entered the premises and opened fire," Thamsanqa Ntuli, the premier of KwaZulu-Natal province, of which Durban is the main city, told AFP.
Three other people survived the attack in the township of KwaMakhutha south of Durban, police said.
The motive for the shooting was not immediately clear, police said, adding that investigators were following a "promising" lead that could assist in the case.
"The incident has left the community in profound shock and grief," Ntuli said.
Local television station eNCA reported that the attackers forced everyone into a room before shooting them and also set fire to a car belonging to one of the victims.
"It's shocking and sad. These are guys I grew up with. I can't believe it. It's like a movie," the broadcaster cited a local resident as saying.
"I've been staying here all my life, and I've never seen anything like this," he added.
Acting police chief Puleng Dimpane said she had activated a 72-hour tracking operation to pursue and apprehend those responsible.
"There is no place in our communities for the senseless taking of human lives. Police must act decisively, mobilise all available resources and pursue those responsible until they are brought before the courts," she said in a statement.
South Africa has one of the world's highest murder rates, with about 60 people killed each day in a country of around 62 million.
In March, soldiers were deployed to violence hotspots across the country to support police efforts to tackle rampant crime, which President Cyril Ramaphosa has described as one of the biggest threats facing South Africa.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Conference of Rulers asked to scrutinise Negri Ruler's removal, Undang Luak dismissals
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Conference of Rulers has been asked to scrutinise and advise on the issue surrounding the removal of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir from the throne, as well as the dismissal of Undang Luak.
The Negri Sembilan Malay Customary Lawyers' Bar (Secretariat), in a joint statement, said the issue should not be confined to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, but should also take into account the dismissal of the Undang Luak.
"We respectfully seek the Conference of Rulers' consideration to scrutinise the process that has taken place to assess and advise whether every action taken, particularly concerning the removal and succession of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undang Luak, was carried out in accordance with the Negri Sembilan Constitution (UUTKNS) 1959 and the rule of law," it said.
The secretariat said the request for advice from the Conference of Rulers should be distinguished from any attempt to assume the functions of the state authorities under the UUTKNS 1959.
It said under such an approach, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia and the Conference of Rulers would not replace the functions of the relevant authorities, but instead review the matter, provide advice and ensure that the process complied with the law.
"This role can be seen as part of the interpretation of the Federal guarantee under Article 71(1) and (2) of the Federal Constitution, particularly in circumstances that have reached a critical stage such as the present situation," it said.
The secretariat, represented by lawyers Emirul Sarifudin Nor Azmi, Asmawi Ismail and Deidra Nur Azmi, also stressed that the issue concerning the position of the Rulers in the crisis was not confined to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar alone.
"The dismissal of the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong and other Undang Luak also touches on the position of the Rulers under the interpretation of the UUTKNS 1959, as the Undang Luak also hold such status within the state's constitutional framework.
"Therefore, any party claiming to defend the institution of the Negri Sembilan Rulers should not practise any form of discriminatory treatment between the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undang Luak involved," it said.
In this regard, the secretariat said the Conference of Rulers held a special position in the country's system of government when an issue concerns the position, privileges and dignity of the institution of the Rulers.
The secretariat said any assessment of the crisis involving the position of the Ruler of Negri Sembilan should be based on a comprehensive examination of the actual chronology of events, in line with the provisions of the UUTKNS 1959.
"The crisis should not be assessed solely based on the latest developments, but should instead be viewed as a chain of events beginning with the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) meeting on March 5, followed by developments on April 17, and culminating in the decision by four Undang on April 19.
"Each stage of this process is directly linked to the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undang Luak and needs to be examined sequentially, rather than in isolation," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian arrested over alleged S$500,000 scam in Singapore
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police handed over a Malaysian man to their Singapore counterparts yesterday after he allegedly masterminded a cross-border scam syndicate.
The 27-year-old suspect allegedly masterminded a syndicate involved in government official impersonation scams and money laundering operations in Singapore.
He is said to have used Malaysian runners to collect cash and gold from victims in Singapore.
He was arrested by federal police yesterday in Kuala Lumpur in a joint operation with the Singapore Police Force (SPF).
The suspect, known as 'Da Xiang', which means 'big elephant' in Chinese, was arrested pursuant to a warrant issued by Singapore authorities.
In a statement, the SPF said its Malaysian counterparts handed over the suspect to them on the same day.
The SPF said 'Da Xiang' had recruited and coordinated at least four Malaysians who travelled to Singapore to carry out assignments for the syndicate.
He allegedly met the runners several times in Malaysia, including assigning tasks, coordinating ATM withdrawals and distributing their earnings.
The runners also allegedly brought gold collected from scam victims back to Johor Baru, where they handed the items to him.
He is believed to have been involved in laundering at least S$500,000 (about RM1.56 million) in scam and illicit proceeds.
The suspect was due to be charged in Singapore today with criminal conspiracy to assist another person to retain benefits from criminal conduct under Section 51 of the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992, read with Section 120B of the Penal Code 1871.
The offence carries a maximum 10-year jail term, a fine of up to S$500,000, or both.
Singapore police said Malaysians travelling to Singapore to assist scam syndicates in collecting cash and valuables from victims was an increasing trend.
SPF Cyber Command commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Justin Wong said the arrest demonstrated the importance of cross-border cooperation between Malaysian and Singaporean authorities.
"Scam syndicates know no borders," he said, thanking Malaysian police for their cooperation in apprehending the alleged mastermind.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chinese tourist drowns while snorkelling in Sabah
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A Chinese tourist in her 30s drowned while snorkelling off Pulau Mengalum here today.
The woman was part of a group of 17 tourists who had travelled by boat to the island for the activity.
Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said police received a report on the incident at about 1.30pm.
"Based on preliminary information, the victim is believed to have drowned while snorkelling in waters about 1.5 metres deep.
"She had been snorkelling for about 15 minutes before a boat crew member monitoring the tourists noticed her floating unconscious.
"The victim was brought ashore and given cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but showed no response. She was later pronounced dead by a medical officer," he said when contacted.
Shahrudin said police who inspected the scene found no criminal element and had recorded statements from witnesses to assist investigations.
He said the case was currently classified as sudden death.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 18-year-old remanded over alleged sexual assault of 16-year-old girl
Article:
KANGAR: Police have detained an 18-year-old unemployed man after he was alleged to have sexually assaulted a 16-year-old girl in Taman Bukit Kubu, Kuala Perlis, last month.
Kangar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the suspect was detained after the girl lodged a report at the Kuala Perlis police station yesterday.
He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred around 2am on Aug 29, when the girl was with the suspect at a friend's house.
"The victim and the suspect went to the side of the house before the suspect allegedly committed the sexual offence against her.
"The victim, who is still a student, said it was the first time they had engaged in such an act before she moved to Sungai Korok, Kedah, on Sept 1," he said in a statement today.
Yusharifuddin said police had issued a medical examination form (Pol 59), and the girl was scheduled to undergo a medical examination at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) in Kangar tomorrow morning.
Meanwhile, at the Magistrate's Court, the suspect was remanded for seven days from today to facilitate investigations.
Magistrate Nurul Natasha Rizal allowed the remand application by the investigating officer.
The suspect, who is from Yan, Kedah, is being investigated under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 (Act 792).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea appears to have tested upgraded hypersonic weapon: Analysts
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea appears to have tested a hypersonic weapon that could evade missile defences and prove hard to track and intercept, analysts told AFP Wednesday.
South Korea and Japan said Pyongyang fired two short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast Sunday, condemning the launches as threats to regional peace and security.
North Korea did not identify the weapon, saying only that its missile bureau had "successfully tested a new type of weapon" in a demonstration of "ultra-modern defence technology."
Analysts said the weapon appeared to be an upgraded version of North Korea's Hwasongpho-11Ma-1 hypersonic short-range ballistic missile.
With a range of 450 to 600 kilometres, the hypersonic missile is "designed to strike key military facilities across the Korean peninsula within an extremely short period of time", Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AFP.
Images released by Pyongyang's state media showed leader Kim Jong Un and his daughter Ju Ae watching a screen displaying what appeared to be the missile's flight path, labelled "Hwasongpho-11Ma-1 flight trajectory."
The North Korean leader warned this week that the weapon's advances would give adversaries "an incurable headache and a very cruel and unavoidable blow", according to the official Korean Central News Agency.
Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its leaders repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.
North Korea has also secured critical backing from Russia alongside its traditional ally China, leaving fewer incentives for it to engage in renewed diplomacy with Washington.
"North Korea may be talking up its own capabilities, but it has clearly reached the point where it can launch weapons of this calibre," Ahn Chan-il, a researcher originally from North Korea, told AFP.
"I believe these tests are less about upgrading its own military capabilities than testing weapons produced by its defence industry to meet Russia's wartime demand."
Since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, North Korea has become a key ally of the Kremlin, sending troops to support Moscow's war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology, analysts say.
Hong Sung-pyo, senior researcher at the Seoul-based Korea Institute for Military Affairs, said that if used against South Korea, the hypersonic weapon would pose a serious threat.
"But a single successful test is not enough to prove its capabilities. If deployed operationally, however, it would be extremely difficult to defend against," he told AFP.
"Because it manoeuvres as it descends during the terminal phase of flight, it is harder to track and intercept than a conventional ballistic missile – particularly at hypersonic speeds."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No suspension notice received' — Negri state legal adviser reports to work
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal reported for work as usual today despite the state government announcing her immediate suspension yesterday.
Muzalmah said she was complying with the directive from Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar to remain and serve in Negri Sembilan.
"I was not prevented from entering the office and am now working as usual without any interference.
"As long as the attorney-general directs me to continue working here (Negri Sembilan), I will continue to carry out my duties as usual.
"Actually, I myself did not receive any official letter informing me that my duties as state legal adviser had been suspended as claimed. I only found out through news reports in the media," she said when contacted.
Muzalmah said civil servants are subject to federal-level directives, hence she would comply with the decisions concerning her.
Attorney-General Dusuki today instructed Muzalmah and Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim to c
ontinue performing their duties
as usual, saying the menteri besar and state executive council's decision to
suspend them yesterday with immediate effect
was invalid.
He said the two senior state government officers could not be prevented from entering their offices to work, as doing so would be unlawful.
Last night, the
A-GC said the Negri Sembilan state executive council
has no legal authority to suspend the state secretary and state legal adviser.
It said matters relating to the appointment, including the suspension of the two office-holders, fall under the jurisdiction of the Public Service Commission and the Judicial and Legal Service Commission.
It said this was provided for under Article 37 of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sepang Aircraft lands 12-year Cebu Pacific MRO contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sepang Aircraft Engineering Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Airbus, has secured a 12-year aircraft maintenance contract from Philippine carrier Cebu Pacific covering seven A320 aircraft.
The contract, announced at the MRO Asia-Pacific event in Singapore yesterday, involves heavy maintenance and end-of-lease (EOL) checks.
The work  is scheduled to be carried out at Sepang Aircraft's facility at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) between 2027 and 2028.
The agreement expands an existing relationship between Sepang Aircraft and Cebu Pacific.
The former has previously carried out heavy maintenance and ad hoc EOL checks, engine changes and skin panel replacement work for the airline.
Sepang Aircraft has also occasionally deployed engineers to Manila to support Cebu Pacific's aircraft maintenance requirements.
Sepang Aircraft general manager and Airbus country representative for Malaysia Burhanudin Noordin Ali said the latest contract reflected the airline's confidence in its maintenance capabilities.
"This latest agreement is a clear sign of trust and confidence placed by the carrier in the work we do," he said.
Cebu Pacific vice-president for engineering and fleet management Shevantha Weerasekera said the partnership would support the carrier's A320 fleet maintenance and airworthiness requirements.
The EOL checks will be conducted as the aircraft are prepared for return to their lessors, ensuring they meet the required maintenance and airworthiness standards before redelivery.
Sepang Aircraft specialises in maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) services for commercial aircraft, engines and components.
Its facilities at KLIA comprise two hangars with a combined area of about 50,000 square metres, with capacity to accommodate up to eight aircraft at a time for major maintenance checks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for KL, 10 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds for Kuala Lumpur and 10 states this afternoon.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected states were Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Kedah, the warning covers Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, it affects Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak.
The warning also covers Jeli and Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kemaman, Dungun, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; and Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut, Lipis and Kuantan in Pahang.
In Selangor, the affected areas are Petaling, Gombak and Hulu Langat, while in Negri Sembilan, the warning covers Jelebu and Jempol.
In Johor, the areas affected are Kulai, Kluang, Kota Tinggi, Mersing, Johor Bahru, Batu Pahat, Muar, Tangkak and Segamat.
In Sabah, the warning covers Kinabatangan in Sandakan; Lahad Datu, Tawau and Kalabakan in Tawau; Pensiangan, Tambunan, Tenom, Membakut, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu, Keningau and Sipitang in the Interior; and the West Coast.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Limbang and Bario, Marudi and Telang Usan in Miri.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Upstream players seek closer Petronas ties amid uncertainties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's upstream oil and gas industry is seeking closer engagement with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) to strengthen the sector's operating environment amid growing geopolitical and supply-chain uncertainties.
The Petroleum Production Sharing Contractors (PPSC) Committee under the Malaysian International Chamber of Commerce & Industry (Micci) recently held its annual engagement with Petronas through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM).
The engagement brought together upstream production sharing contractors and industry representatives to discuss key issues affecting the sector.
Micci PPSC Committee convenor Ben Kwa said continued engagement between industry players and the regulator was important as the upstream sector operates in an increasingly complex environment.
"The PPSC provides a platform for members to raise matters affecting the sector, share industry perspectives and work with relevant stakeholders towards continuous improvement and mutual benefit," he said in a statement.
Discussions covered operational and supply-chain preparedness amid geopolitical uncertainty, as well as the need for sustained investment, capability development, safety and continued industry collaboration to support Malaysia's upstream competitiveness.
The engagement also reviewed progress in key areas including fiscal and economic matters, procurement, exploration, decarbonisation, talent development and operations.
Established in 1988, the PPSC comprises 24 upstream production sharing contractors, including operators and non-operators.
It serves as a platform for members to represent common interests and engage with the industry regulator and the government on matters affecting the upstream oil and gas sector.
"Through regular engagements and constructive dialogue, industry stakeholders continue to advance shared priorities, improve industry practices and strengthen local capabilities, including efforts to build a sustainable talent pipeline for Malaysia's upstream sector.
"These collaborative efforts are contributing to shaping a competitive, resilient and sustainable upstream industry, while building the capabilities and talent needed to support Malaysia's long-term energy aspirations," the committee said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says PH open to talks with any party ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
HANGZHOU: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to talks with any party ahead of the Melaka state election, including Bersatu.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the coalition's openness was for the good of the country's political landscape.
He said arrogance and a refusal to negotiate should be avoided in politics when a party expressed willingness to hold talks.
"I have tasked Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and he is now holding discussions. We should not be arrogant. If someone says they are ready to talk, we talk. That is how politics works.
"Some people say, oh, we do not want this. No. Discuss the issues. Whether we agree or disagree is up to the committee," he told reporters aboard a high-speed train from Shanghai to the city today.
Earlier, Anwar, who is also PH chairman, delivered the keynote address at the opening of the Plenary Session of the WorldSkills Conference 2026 in Shanghai, which was officiated by Chinese Premier Li Qiang.
He was responding to media questions about speculation that PH could form political cooperation with Bersatu.
PH had yet to make any final decision on cooperation with other parties, including Barisan Nasional, Anwar said.
He said he intended to continue focusing on serving the country during the remaining 15 months of his administration.
"I hope God gives me good health for the remaining period. I want to continue working," he said.

Title: Seat allocation remains key issue ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seat allocation remains a key unresolved issue among political blocs ahead of the Melaka state election, with parties still working to reach an agreement.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Barisan Nasional wanted to retain the 21 seats it won in the 2021 state election, leaving limited room for potential partners.
He said any agreement would also depend on whether the parties could convince their grassroots machinery to accept the arrangement and campaign together.
"Leadership matters, but the immediate test is whether they can agree on seats and campaign together," he said.
Tawfik said several arrangements remained possible, including a BN-Perikatan Nasional understanding to avoid direct contests and vote-splitting in selected constituencies.
He said BN-Pakatan Harapan cooperation was also possible as the two blocs work together in the federal government, although Melaka PH had recently said it had yet to hold talks with BN.
He said an understanding between PH and Bersatu could also emerge, while BN, PH and PN could contest separately if negotiations failed.
Tawfik said the state government's record, national political alignments, local issues and candidates could influence the contest, particularly in closely fought seats.
He described the election as an important test of BN-PH cooperation, saying any electoral pact would require the parties to agree on seats, persuade their grassroots to campaign together and explain the arrangement to voters.
For BN, he said an understanding with PN could reduce the risk of the two blocs competing for the same pool of voters, although negotiations would be complicated by BN's intention to defend its 21 seats.
For PH, cooperation with BN could provide a route to sharing power in Melaka, provided it secured a meaningful number of winnable seats.
Meanwhile, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the political cooperation model adopted during the Negri Sembilan election should serve as a basis for future cooperation, including in the general election.
Describing the model, in which BN and PN formed a political alliance, as one of the best examples of cooperation, he said there were still several areas that could be explored.
"Discussions should not be limited to the allocation of state seats; they could also include parliamentary seats and appointed seats, where applicable," he said.
On seat allocation, Tuan Ibrahim said the matter would be left to the state-level seat negotiation committee, with the final decision to be made by the respective parties.
"I expect the matter to be finalised in the near future, pending feedback from the Election Commission on the important dates for the state election," he said.

Title: In Bangladesh, Pakistan's Jinnah photo stirs anger
Article:
PAKISTAN founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah died nearly eight decades ago, but his photograph has become the centrepiece of a fresh battle over history at Bangladesh's top university.
The image of Jinnah was shown at a new museum display this month at Dhaka University – only to be torn down, exposing a bitter dispute over how Bangladesh remembers its complicated history.
Abu Tayyab Habildar, the university student who ripped the photograph, called Jinnah a "villain."
The row shows how the legacies of nationality, religion and language that shaped Bangladesh are politically potent – and how the 2024 revolution that toppled Sheikh Hasina has upended old narratives.
Pakistan and Bangladesh were once the western and eastern wings of a single country, created by the violent partition of British-ruled India in 1947.
They were separated by more than 1,500 kilometres (930 miles) of Indian territory.
Bangladesh won independence from Pakistan after a bitter 1971 war, during which Pakistani forces were accused of widespread atrocities.
Hundreds of thousands were killed – Bangladeshi estimates say millions – and many in Dhaka still demand Islamabad apologise for the killings.
Jinnah was not an Islamist, but his campaign for a separate Muslim homeland makes him a potent symbol for Bangladesh's opposition Islamist politicians, who seek to emphasise the country's Muslim identity.
"In Bangladesh, Jinnah was never celebrated," said political analyst Altaf Parvez.
"The ground is fertile for the rise of the Islamists. They need a suitable leader, and that is why there is so much fuss around Jinnah."
The Dhaka University Central Students Union (DUCSU), led by Bangladesh Chhatra Shibir, the student wing of the country's largest Islamist political party, said the photograph was part of a chronological display tracing the university's history.
DUCSU leader SM Farhad criticised what he called the "mob attack" that ripped the picture down.
"You can correct us if we make any mistake, though we haven't made any," he told AFP.
Critics accused the student union of trying to reshape that history by highlighting Jinnah – while diminishing Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, Bangladesh's founding president and independence leader.
"Jinnah is the father of Pakistan," Habildar, the student who ripped the picture down, told AFP.
"But that same Jinnah, when he stood against Bengali and Bangla language, he is a villain."
But Rahman's legacy is also deeply controversial.
His daughter is Sheikh Hasina, whose iron-fisted rule as prime minister ended in a bloody student-led 2024 revolution, and is reviled by those who overthrew her.
Hasina has been sentenced to death in absentia, and activities of her former ruling Awami League have been banned.
Rahman's former home, later turned into a museum, was torched during the uprising.
Farhad, the DUCSU leader, said the university museum also needed an update.
"They left no stone unturned to establish the narrative of the Awami League... so we thought we would renovate it," he said.
But student Mahafuzur Rahman, 19, said removing photographs was not the answer.
"I don't think it's good to remove his photo... He is also part of history."
The space where Jinnah's photograph hung remains empty.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen assaulted mother days before fatal Bandar Utama school stabbing — psychiatric report
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Just 13 days before a 15-year-old boy fatally stabbed his 16-year-old schoolmate at a Bandar Utama school last year, he assaulted his mother when she tried to inspect his bag.
The boy had pushed her, causing her to fall and hit her head.
The incident was revealed in a psychiatric report by Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta director and forensic consultant psychiatrist Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony.
It was contained in the 77-page grounds of judgment by High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid.
"The incident occurred when his mother attempted to check his school bag, having noticed that he was wearing two layers of clothing to school and carrying extra clothing and a cap in his bag.
"He was also angry at being forced to attend therapy," said Ian Lloyd.
The boy had been seeing a school counsellor following repeated complaints that he was coming late to school, sleeping in class and having long hair.
The counsellor referred him for private therapy, but none of the four sessions was productive as he remained guarded, uninterested and suspicious throughout, and would hide his face inside his T-shirt or behind his palms.
Ian Lloyd's psychiatric report identified a further evolution of the boy's psychotic symptoms in 2023.
The boy became suspicious that closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras had been secretly installed in his home.
The teen described feeling watched by the eye of the technician who had installed the CCTV, whom he believed was a pervert monitoring him remotely.
"The report referred to this as a paranoid delusion reinforced by his perception of a red light in his room, recorded as a visual hallucination. He came to believe his parents had covertly installed cameras in his room and bathroom, and was convinced that he was being spied upon.
"By early 2025, this belief had extended to the school environment. The child believed the school security guard was covertly watching him on CCTV from the guard post and that certain teachers were doing likewise.
"He believed cameras observed him even while he was hiding in the school washroom.
"The same conviction extended to public spaces such as shopping malls, which he believed contained cameras specifically directed at monitoring him. The report recorded this as paranoid delusions and delusions of reference," he said.
Ian Lloyd said the same delusional beliefs appeared to explain his chronic lateness to school.
"Each morning upon arrival at school, the boy would remain seated in the car with his mother for a further 20 to 30 minutes after his brother had gone in.
"He also insisted that the car be parked away from the entrance of the school, and would scan his surroundings for safety before alighting.
"He avoided Monday assemblies by hiding in the male washroom, at times remaining in a washroom cubicle for up to two hours, before returning to class. The report attributed the conduct to paranoid and persecutory delusions."
On Sept 14, the boy was acquitted of murdering his schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama. The High Court found him to have been of
unsound mind during the incident.
Adlin ordered the boy to be detained and treated at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar slams MB, state exco move to remove Negri Sembilan Ruler
Article:
HANGZHOU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the move by Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and the state executive councilors to remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir from the throne as disrespectful and uncivilised.
Anwar stressed that no one in the state administration had the power or mandate to take such action.
"The menteri besar and state exco made the decision. This is disrespectful, uncivilised and I strongly object. Since when did they have the mandate to question the position of the Ruler?" he said to reporters while travelling by high-speed train from Shanghai to Hangzhou today.
Ismail had previously confirmed that the
proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz
as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan was decided and unanimously endorsed by the state exco.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the federal government was not interfering in the issue.
He explained that his decision
to seek an audience
with Tuanku Muhriz recently was made because the court had ruled that he was the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
He said while the power to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar from the throne was subject to the decision of the Undang Luak, such a decision was not absolute and had to comply with the relevant rules.
"I respect the Undang, and I know some of them well. But they have to understand that we are not interfering. We have to safeguard the country. National security and the institutions are our responsibility. Don't say that we cannot interfere; this is not interference.
"The Undang cannot simply make a decision. Their decision is not absolute; they too have to follow the rules. Now we are hearing both sides. There are two sides — one Undang says he is the Undang, while another says he is not.
"We have the Luak and views saying otherwise. So I said, decide first. If all the Undang have followed the proper process and the Undang appointed makes a decision, that is outside my jurisdiction," he said.

Title: KLIA still Asia Pacific's most connected megahub, retains 4th spot globally
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has retained its position as Asia Pacific's most connected megahub and the world's fourth most connected international airport, according to OAG's 2026 Megahubs Index.
OAG said KLIA's capacity grew 6.9 per cent, supported by an expanding airline network that has added seven new scheduled carriers and nine new routes so far this year.
The new links include Riyadh, Algeria and Jinan, while Malaysia Airlines has strengthened connectivity with Japan through its new direct Fukuoka-Kuala Lumpur service.
Further expansion is expected with Gulf Air, Hainan Airlines, Zipair, Thai Vietjet and Lufthansa scheduled to begin or resume services later this year.
Lufthansa is set to return in October with five weekly Frankfurt-Kuala Lumpur services.
Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said KLIA's growth must be matched by improvements in capacity and passenger experience.
"KLIA's standing among the world's most connected Megahubs reflects the strength and breadth of our aviation network, built through the combined efforts of our airline partners, airport teams and industry stakeholders," he said.
"But growth is meaningful only when it is matched by the right experience and the right capacity to support it. That is why our focus at KLIA goes beyond connectivity. We are working across the entire passenger journey to make KLIA more convenient, efficient and welcoming."
He said Malaysia Airports aimed to further strengthen KLIA's position as Asia Pacific's most connected Megahub while ensuring service standards kept pace with its growth.
The airport has rolled out a range of upgrades, including improved check-in and self-service baggage drop facilities, enhanced kerbside traffic management through the Vehicle Access Management System and a new e-hailing system at Terminal 1.
Other improvements include additional passenger trolleys, complimentary wheelchairs and baby strollers, family-friendly facilities, as well as a Calm Room and Harimau Playground at Terminal 2.
New attractions such as Rimba and Heritage Walls are also adding nature and culture-inspired elements to the passenger experience.

Title: Foul smell, black water raise concerns over Sungai Sengkuang
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A foul smell from Sungai Sengkuang, an offshoot of Sungai Tebrau located just 5km from the country's entry point, has raised concerns among residents and motorists using the Eastern Dispersal Link (EDL).
Residents in nearby areas, including Taman Sri Stulang, Kampung Tengah and Taman Iskandar, said the stench persisted regardless of the tide, while the river water had also turned black.
PPR Sri Stulang resident Ain Mohd Sulaiman, 30, said the worsening stench had affected residents' daily lives, with the smell entering their homes.
"We do not know whether the smell comes from sewage discharged from a nearby treatment plant.
"We are worried about the possible impact on our families, especially children and the elderly," she said.
Batu Puteri resident Arif Atan, 52, said the river remained dirty and foul-smelling despite machines being deployed to collect floating rubbish.
He said authorities should adopt more effective measures to address the pollution, which was also affecting motorists using the EDL.
"Imagine residents having to endure the smell every day. It could also affect the city's image," he said.
Bumi Hijau Johor Environmental Care Association chairman P. Siva Kumar said the pollution should be treated seriously, as prolonged contamination could damage the river and create wider environmental problems.
He said the state government and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage should identify the source of the pollution and take action against those responsible.
"Every river in Johor should be protected as rivers are a source of water supply, especially as Johor needs sufficient water to support data centres and other industries," he said.
He also called for more effective cleaning methods or alternative technologies if conventional measures failed to resolve the problem.
Two years ago, four tributaries of Sungai Tebrau — Sungai Pandan, Sungai Sebulung, Sungai Sengkuang and Sungai Tampoi — were reported to have recorded worrying water quality, with sewage, industrial, commercial and earthwork activities cited among the sources of pollution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar post-coup leader says 'lenient' on Suu Kyi: Report
Article:
YANGON: Myanmar's coup leader turned civilian president Min Aung Hlaing said in an interview published Wednesday he has been "extremely lenient" on Aung San Suu Kyi, who he ousted and jailed in 2021.
Min Aung Hlaing ordered the military putsch that toppled the Nobel Peace Prize laureate's democratic government, claiming she won power through massive voter fraud in elections the previous year.
Suu Kyi remains detained on charges rights groups say were confected to return power to the military, which has historically ruled Myanmar since independence.
"I have been extremely lenient toward her," Min Aung Hlaing said, according to an interview with US magazine Time.
"We made every possible effort to prevent the situation from reaching this point."
Min Aung Hlaing retired as military chief to become civilian president in April, following elections derided by rights groups as a charade.
He has since been on a diplomatic push to end Myanmar's international pariah status, but many nations remain concerned about the 81-year-old Suu Kyi.
Analysts say Min Aung Hlaing is using the prospect of loosening her detention to entice countries into engaging – despite a raging civil war challenging his rule.
Just days before he made a landmark trip to Thailand in August, his office released rare photos showing Suu Kyi meeting with a senior Red Cross official.
The possibility of an amnesty for Suu Kyi "depends on her", the president told Time, but hinted the situation may change if "grounds for reconsideration emerge on our part."
Min Aung Hlaing personally ordered Suu Kyi be moved from jail to house arrest in the capital Naypyidaw in April, as he prepared to make his push for international recognition.
The December-January election installing Min Aung Hlaing was tightly controlled by his junta, sidelined Suu Kyi's party and punished dissenters with prison time.
Analysts described his nominally civilian administration as a proxy of the military.
"There are various forms of democracy," Min Aung Hlaing said in the Time interview.
"There is American democracy, there is European democracy.
"I will ensure that Myanmar achieves a democratic system that truly aligns with our own culture, customs, and traditions."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines extends Airbus support for A330 fleet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has extended its flight hour services (FHS) contract with Airbus for its A330ceo fleet, reinforcing a maintenance partnership that has been in place since 2017.
The agreement, announced yesterday at the MRO Asia Pacific event in Singapore, provides long-term, power-by-the-hour support covering component services, on-site stock, pool access, repairs and component reliability engineering.
Malaysia Airlines will also have access to Airbus' engineering expertise and regional FHS representatives to support its day-to-day maintenance operations.
The extension makes Airbus FHS the primary maintenance support programme for the airline's A330ceo fleet, while the arrangement also covers its newer A330neo aircraft, which entered service in 2024.
Malaysia Airlines chief operating officer Aida Salfaraz Ahmad Fadzil said the extension reflects the value the programme continues to deliver to the airline.
"The extension of this agreement reflects the value that the Airbus Flight Hour Services programme continues to bring to our operations."
Since 2017, Airbus has supported the performance and reliability of our A330 fleet through its component services and technical expertise, he added.
"As we continue to focus on operational efficiency and service excellence, this programme remains an important part of our support framework, and we look forward to continuing our collaboration with Airbus," Aida said.
Airbus Asia Pacific president Anand Stanley said the extension reflected Malaysia Airlines' confidence in the FHS programme.
"This A330ceo contract extension is a strong testament to the trust Malaysia Airlines places in the Airbus Flight Hour Services programme," he said.
"We have been working closely with Malaysia Airlines for almost a decade to enhance our services activities, and look forward to continuing to support the performance and reliability of its A330 fleet."
Airbus said its FHS programme is designed to help airlines maximise fleet performance while controlling operational costs through integrated maintenance support.
The programme combines Airbus' engineering expertise, technology and data-driven insights to improve component availability, maintenance efficiency and fleet reliability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippine Senate lowers threshold to oust VP Duterte
Article:
MANILA: The Philippine Senate approved on Wednesday a lower threshold of votes needed to find Vice President Sara Duterte guilty at her impeachment trial, potentially making it easier to execute her ouster.
Senators voted 13-1, with six Duterte allies abstaining, that the constitutionally required two-thirds guilty verdict by "all members of the Senate" refers only to those "capable of participating."
At least four senators loyal to the vice president, including two now in jail, are now absent from the impeachment proceedings.
On Wednesday, presiding judge Senator Francis Escudero said the decision, which effectively lowers the number of guilty votes needed from 16 to 14, would be treated as the "controlling ruling" going forward.
"While the chair takes exception to this decision, the chair nonetheless accepts it as a judgment of this court and is bound to give it effect," said Escudero, who was the sole "no" vote.
Duterte's lawyers can still appeal the lower threshold at the Supreme Court.
"We accept the decision without waiving our right to go up to the Supreme Court.... From today until the (verdict), many things can still happen," said Duterte defence counsel Michael Poa.
Vice presidential spokesperson Paolo Panelo called Wednesday's vote an attempt at "changing the constitution."
"Their aim is to manufacture a conviction. They cannot get 16, so they want to lower (it) to convict VP Sara," he said.
The House of Representatives impeached Duterte on May 11 on allegations of graft, corruption, bribery and an alleged assassination plot against one-time ally President Ferdinand Marcos.
Should the Senate find her guilty, she will be stripped of the vice presidency and permanently barred from elected office.
Two of Duterte's allies are currently in prison on corruption charges and another is hiding while sought on an International Criminal Court warrant.
A fourth, who is out of the country seeking medical treatment, is under investigation.
But they are not alone. Five other senators in the Duterte camp are currently the subject of government probes.
Cleve Arguelles of pollster WR Numero told AFP ahead of the vote that "given the pressure Malacanang (the presidential palace) appears to be exerting on Duterte allies in the Senate, the working expectation is that the administration will continue trying to secure 16 votes."
Arguelles added he believed there was a "strong likelihood" that number could be reached even if the lowered threshold made it unnecessary.
Marcos has repeatedly denied having any influence on the impeachment process.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM takes high-speed train to Hangzhou after Shanghai event
Article:
SHANGHAI: After delivering his keynote address at the Plenary Session of the WorldSkills Shanghai, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Malaysian delegation hurried to Hangzhou.
However, the prime minister opted to travel to Hangzhou, about 170km from Shanghai, by high-speed train.
Anwar, together with the government delegation and media personnel, boarded the high-speed train from Hongqiao Station at 11.50am and arrived at Hangzhou East Station at 1.06pm.
During the roughly one-hour journey, the prime minister also took the opportunity to chat with media personnel, sharing his views and updates on various developments in the country.
Among the issues discussed were the customary and administrative crisis in Negri Sembilan, Anthony Loke's decision to resign as transport minister and the pardon involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
While commenting on the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly, Anwar jokingly sang a line from a song, which was met with laughter from the media personnel and delegates accompanying him.
Upon arriving in Hangzhou, Anwar was welcomed by Hangzhou Executive Deputy Mayor Xu Wenguang.
Also on the journey were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Loke and Malaysia's Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.
In Hangzhou today, Anwar is scheduled to attend bilateral meetings with six industry leaders before attending a dinner hosted by Chinese Premier Li Qiang.
The prime minister is then scheduled to attend the launch of the Mandarin translation of the book 'Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform, and Ignorance in Postnormal Times'.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 81pct of developers report higher business costs in 1H 2026 [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia's market survey showed that 81 per cent of respondents reported higher costs of doing business in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), up from 74 per cent in the second half of 2025 (2H 2025).
The survey, which involved 181 respondents, indicated that among those reporting higher costs, 35 per cent recorded an increase of between three and six per cent.
Rehda president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said construction costs had risen by an average of about 13 per cent, although the impact varied depending on the type of construction work.
"For earthworks and infrastructure works, they experienced a rise of about 20 per cent to 30 per cent, but for normal building works, some of it is even as low as about three to five per cent," he said at a media briefing on Rehda's Property Industry Survey for the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) here today.
Zaini said the increase was partly driven by higher prices for diesel-related products, including bitumen, following the Middle East conflict, which particularly affected road, earthworks and infrastructure projects.
The survey also showed that 63 per cent of respondents faced construction challenges in 1H 2026, with high material prices, supply shortages and inconsistent supply cited as the top three building material-related challenges.
On labour, the top three challenges were high wages, shortage of labour supply and lack of skilled workers.
Zaini said ongoing projects should generally be able to be completed within their existing budgets, while contracts for new projects could be priced slightly higher to account for increased costs.
He said contracts would typically have a contingency of about three to five per cent to accommodate cost increases.
Despite the Middle East conflict, Zaini does not expect another significant jump in construction material prices as prices have begun to stabilise following the initial increase.
"Prices went up significantly due to the Middle East crisis. Now, you can see that prices have already stabilised.
"Although the war continues, I do not really expect such a big jump in construction material prices because currently they have already absorbed the first tranche of higher prices," he said.
In the outlook for the housing market, Zaini indicated that buyers are likely to remain cautious during the first half of 2027, depending on developments in the Middle East conflict, although developers will continue to provide homes across various market segments.
"Despite the Middle East conflict, people still need houses. So, we have to provide a range of homes between the affordable, middle-class and higher-end segments because each segment has its respective buyers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cambodia no 'safe haven' for cyberscams, PM says
Article:
PHNOM PENH: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet told an anti-fraud summit Wednesday that his country would never be a "safe haven" for cyberscams, as international partners touted law enforcement successes but warned more must be done.
Southeast Asia, especially Cambodia and war-torn Myanmar, has emerged as a hub for crime syndicates running centres filled with scammers – some willing, some trafficked – who defraud internet users through fake romantic relationships or cryptocurrency investment schemes.
"Cambodia will never be a safe haven for online scams," Hun Manet told a conference against online scams organised by his government in the capital Phnom Penh.
He said Cambodian authorities had "completely dismantled all light-scale scam compounds" in a high-profile crackdown launched last year.
He denied the move was a "public relations campaign", saying it was focused on "permanently eradicating criminal networks and preventing their re-emergence."
Cambodia acted under pressure from key ally China as well as the United States, after years of accusations that it allowed scam centres to thrive, generating billions of dollars in illicit profits annually.
But researchers say scammers have dispersed to smaller, lower-profile locations, while in many cases centres were given advance warning of raids.
Delphine Schantz, regional representative of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), hailed Cambodia's efforts but said "more can be done and needs to be done" at national, regional and international levels.
Yang Weilin, Chinese vice minister of public security, also praised Cambodia's cooperation with Beijing, saying "no country can stay immune, or tackle the problem single-handedly."
Yet "we must be sober-minded that the breeding ground for telecom fraud has not been fully rooted out", he told the conference.
FBI official Stephen Flores said law enforcement partnerships needed to be based on "trust and shared sacrifice."
The United States estimates that in 2025 alone, transnational criminal organisations in Southeast Asia defrauded Americans out of at least US$18.2 billion through cyber-enabled scams.
Visiting Phnom Penh in July, FBI Director Kash Patel said online scams were a "top priority", urging "increased efforts to hold high-level scam bosses accountable", and more information sharing on "complicit officials."
Analysts say elite protection networks and the financial and physical infrastructure of the scam industry remains intact, raising concerns that operators can regroup.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Medini gains another GBS tenant as Teleperformance expands Malaysian footprint
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Investment Bhd (IIB) says Teleperformance has opened a new operation at Menara IIB in Medini, Johor, strengthening the area's position as a regional global business services (GBS) hub.
The new facility expands Teleperformance's Malaysian footprint beyond Kuala Lumpur and Penang, supporting customer experience, digital operations and revenue services for businesses in Singapore and across Southeast Asia.
IIB president and chief executive officer Datuk Idzham Mohd Hashim said Teleperformance's presence adds to Medini's growing business ecosystem and strengthens its proposition as a base for regional operations.
"For IIB, Teleperformance's presence is another step in strengthening Medini as an end-to-end business ecosystem where companies can establish, operate and grow," he said.
Idzham said companies needed more than office space, including access to talent, business support, housing and commercial amenities for employees.
"Bringing these elements together is key to creating an environment where businesses can grow for the long term," he said.
Medini is located within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), benefiting from its proximity to Singapore and connectivity to the wider Johor-Singapore economic corridor.
IIB said 47 GBS companies have established operations in Medini since 2013, supporting about 7,200 jobs.
The ecosystem includes companies such as Startek Malaysia, Vistra, Deluxe Games Inc, Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd (Etiqa) and Katoen Natie Sdn Bhd.
Teleperformance's latest operation is expected to further expand the employment base and add capabilities to the GBS ecosystem.
IIB said the growing concentration of GBS players was helping deepen the local talent pool, strengthen business networks and generate demand for local services and suppliers.
Initiatives such as GBS Iskandar@Medini are also aimed at connecting businesses, industry partners and stakeholders to support the sector's development.
IIB said the JS-SEZ provides an additional platform for Singapore-based businesses, multinationals and GBS operators to expand capacity while serving regional markets.
